_meta.indication: Treatment of adult and pediatric (newborn and older) patients with primary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) with refractory, recurrent or progressive disease or intolerance with conventional HLH therapy

pivotal_trials.population: 27 pediatric patients (median age 1 year; range 0.2 to 13) with primary HLH refractory, recurrent, or progressive during conventional therapy or intolerant to conventional HLH therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) at end of treatment (complete response, partial response, or HLH improvement), compared to a prespecified null hypothesis of 40%
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 63% (95% CI 0.42, 0.81); p=0.013; complete response 26% (7), partial response 30% (8), HLH improvement 7.4% (2)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%): infections (56%), hypertension (41%), infusion-related reactions (27%), and pyrexia (24%). Serious adverse reactions in 53% of patients; fatal adverse reactions in 2 (6%) patients (septic shock and gastrointestinal hemorrhage). Serious infections observed in 32% of patients.
target_moa: Emapalumab is an IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds and neutralizes free and receptor-bound interferon gamma (IFNγ), a cytokine whose elevated levels are a hallmark of HLH
modality: mAb (recombinant human IgG1 anti-interferon gamma monoclonal antibody)

advisory_committee.vote: Application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the safety data did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues unexpected in the intended population

description.text: Expanded indication to include HLH/MAS in known or suspected Still's disease, including sJIA, with inadequate response or intolerance to glucocorticoids, or with recurrent MAS

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sBLA provides for expansion of the indication to include treatment of adult and pediatric (newborn and older) patients with hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH)/macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) in known or suspected Still's disease, including systemic Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (sJIA), with an inadequate response or intolerance to glucocorticoids, or with recurrent MAS.

summary.text: Emapalumab received Breakthrough Therapy designation (March 11, 2016) and Orphan designation (March 26, 2018), and the BLA was reviewed under Priority review with a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher granted; it received regular (not accelerated) approval based on the ORR observed in single-arm trial NI-0501-04.

citations.quote: Breakthrough designation was granted on March 11, 2016, for patients with pHLH with refractory disease or with recurrent or progressive disease during conventional HLH therapy.
Orphan designation was granted on March 26, 2018, for the treatment of HLH.
We also inform you that you have been granted a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher, as provided under section 529 of the FDCA.

The review teams recommend regular approval of emapalumab under 21 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 601 for the indication "treatment of adult and pediatric (newborn and older) patients with primary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) with refractory, recurrent or progressive disease or intolerance to conventional HLH therapy".
